turns.text: need a short thank you email to ms lugo for reading my personal statement. i emailed her draft 7 yesterday, the marsh one. she only reads one draft per student a week and its fridays so dont make it ask for anything before then

Happy to. Here's a short version:

Subject: Thank you for reading my draft

Hi Ms. Lugo,

Thank you for taking the time to read my personal statement draft. I really appreciate you fitting it in. I'll look forward to your feedback whenever it's ready on Friday.

Thanks again,
[your name]

Want it a bit warmer or more formal?
ok but add something about how its still rough and i'll send a better version soon. back in draft hell lol

I'd leave that out. The draft is already sent, and this email is just a thank-you. Saying it's rough and promising a new version tells her to expect something other than what she's reading, and it might nudge her to hold off on feedback. A teacher reading one draft a week will read what's in front of her.

If you want a light touch of your own, this works:

Hi Ms. Lugo,

Thank you for reading my personal statement draft. I appreciate you making time for it. I'm looking forward to your thoughts on Friday and will work from whatever you suggest.

Thanks again,
[your name]

That shows you're ready to revise without apologizing for what you sent.
genuinely not sure. its nearly 1am and i have to be up at 6:50 lol. can u do one version with a tiny 'i know its not perfect' line so i can compare

Sure, here's the version with it:

Hi Ms. Lugo,

Thank you for reading my personal statement draft. I know it's not perfect, so I'm looking forward to your feedback on Friday and will use it to keep improving it.

Thanks again,
[your name]

The line is framed as being open to feedback, not as an apology, which is the safer way to include it. Compare the two and pick the one that sounds most like you. Either is fine to send in the morning, so you can sleep on it.
Good pick. Send it in the morning and get some sleep. Good luck with the feedback on Friday!
